why: The other half of the same missing evidence, and the half a server gets wrong by being strict. `gage` is not declared here either — nothing is — so a server that validated the filter against a declared set would reject the one class this corpus actually holds, and an agent would be told its correct name was a typo. The filter is read and not judged: it admits the two `gage` nodes, the search finds them, and both `rejected` and `absence` are null because the call was legal and it found something. Without this case the sibling one is satisfiable by a server that rejects every `class` filter on an unschematised corpus and reports `class-undeclared` on the way past.
